There's a key detail in Apple's new Upgrade program: 'If you buy an iPhone with a loan, you must connect it to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon at sign-up.'

John Gruber has a new post over at Daring Fireball today that offers a possible explanation for the requirement.

Apple Upgrade iPhone restrictions

According to a former Apple carrier team employee who spoke with Gruber, the requirement is largely a result of agreements Apple has in place with US Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile.

The agreements Apple negotiates with each carrier are worth "hundreds of millions of dollars," and Apple makes concessions to land them. Requiring iPhones purchased through Apple Upgrade to be connected to T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T accounts appears to be one such concession.

The former Apple employee elaborated on those agreements:

Fraud and risk assessment is another factor. According to a former Apple Store retail employee cited by Gruber, there has been a 'massive spike' in fraudulent iPhone sales since Apple began offering carrier installment plans in its stores.

Apple does note that while your iPhone must be connected to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when you sign up for Apple Upgrade, the phone itself stays unlocked: "To take out a loan on an iPhone, you must select a qualifying carrier (but you cannot use a prepaid carrier plan). Your loaned iPhone stays unlocked, so you can switch carriers at any time, subject to the terms of your chosen carrier."

You can read Gruber's full post at Daring Fireball.
